title: arXiv Mathematics — daily report — 17 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from stated results, scope, cross-field relevance, and methodological evidence, not readership or downloads. Citation evidence for these very recent preprints is limited, and author claims are not independently verified here.

sections.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
sections.abstract: The paper claims that the smoothed regular octagon uniquely minimizes optimal lattice-packing density among centrally symmetric convex planar disks, up to nonsingular affine transformations, using control bounds, local inequalities, and finite verification.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the Reinhardt conjecture, including the equality characterization by nonsingular affine images of the smoothed regular octagon (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane; compare each disk's optimal lattice-packing density.
sections.unique_caveat: The author calls the proof long and explicitly hopes for a shorter proof; the finite verification and full argument remain to be independently checked.
sections.ranking_evidence: A concrete claimed resolution of a classical planar packing conjecture, cross-listed in metric geometry and optimization, with extensive finite verification described in the abstract and paper contents.

sections.title: Generic splitting types and Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines
sections.abstract: For complex projective line arrangements, the authors claim the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle is determined by the intersection lattice through 18 lines, thereby proving Terao's freeness conjecture for 17- and 18-line arrangements and extending a bounded-exponent case to any number of lines.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim lattice-determined generic splitting through 18 lines, Terao for 17 and 18 lines, and freeness invariance for free arrangements whose smaller exponent is at most 8 (paper abstract and Theorems 1.1–1.2, 1.6).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Arrangements of complex projective lines; the stated conjecture cases are 17 and 18 lines, and the all-size extension is limited to the stated smaller-exponent condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof is computer-assisted and the authors explicitly make no positive-characteristic claim; the computations and certificates warrant independent verification.
sections.ranking_evidence: A concrete finite-range conjecture result spanning algebraic geometry and combinatorics; the paper supplies ancillary code, data, and certificates and discusses computation reliability. The introduction notes an independent recent proof for 17 lines, while this paper also treats 18 lines and broader consequences.

sections.title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author claims that no balanced planar polygon can be equidissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles, completing Stein's conjecture beyond the previously treated rational-coordinate case.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims that every balanced polygon in the plane has no equidissection into an odd number of triangles (paper abstract and Theorem 2).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A balanced polygon is one whose oriented boundary vectors in each direction sum to zero; the claim concerns equal-area triangular dissections and odd triangle counts.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is specifically about balanced polygons and parity of equal-area triangular dissections; it does not settle analogous questions for arbitrary polygons.
sections.ranking_evidence: A stated full resolution of a named conjecture with a bridge between polygon dissections, trivalent-graph flows, and number-field valuations; cross-listed in combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: Counterexamples to Grad's conjecture of any knot type
sections.abstract: The authors construct smooth magnetohydrostatic counterexamples in toroidal domains of arbitrary knot type, with nonvanishing magnetic fields and nested pressure tori, and describe families with prescribed flow slopes or twist.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim smooth equilibria violating Grad's conjecture for every toroidal-domain knot type, plus a finite-regularity variant with nonconstant rotational transform (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Magnetohydrostatic equilibria in toroidal domains; the smooth construction has nested pressure tori outside a nondegenerate magnetic axis and a nonvanishing field.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes an existence construction, not stability, robustness, or physical realizability of the equilibria.
sections.ranking_evidence: A sharply stated counterexample construction linking analysis of PDEs and geometric topology, with knot type and flow behavior varied across smooth families.

sections.title: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
sections.abstract: The authors claim that genus-10 curves arising as W(E_6)-covers of the projective line give a 9-dimensional family of counterexamples to Green's canonical-curve syzygy conjecture and to the Green–Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim both conjectures fail on the described genus-10 W(E_6)-cover family (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Canonical syzygies and secant behavior of genus-10 curves that are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexamples lie in a specified special family; the authors say the conjectures remain true generically and in many other cases.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract identifies explicit counterexamples to two conjectures and a 9-dimensional family, linking algebraic geometry and commutative algebra.

sections.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author constructs a compact operator with trace-class self-commutator and vanishing Helton–Howe measure that stays outside the Hilbert–Schmidt class after any bounded stabilization and normal subtraction, yielding counterexamples to two operator-theoretic conjectures.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims a rank-profile obstruction invariant under Hilbert–Schmidt perturbation and normal stabilization, distinguishing the constructed operator from zero (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A compact operator with trace-class self-commutator and zero Helton–Howe measure; the non-approximation assertion is in the Schatten class S₂ under the stated bounded perturbations.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a technically constrained operator counterexample; its hypotheses should not be read as a statement about arbitrary compact operators.
sections.ranking_evidence: A concrete counterexample to both normal dilation and stable classification conjectures, cross-listed in functional analysis and operator algebras and built from finite-torus magnetic shifts.

sections.title: Large gaps and the ten martini problem for monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators
sections.abstract: The authors claim the ten martini theorem for a large class of monotone potentials, using polynomially large spectral gaps for periodic approximations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the ten martini theorem throughout a large class of monotone potentials (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Monotone quasiperiodic potentials; the abstract's scope is the authors' large class, with details in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not enumerate the precise admissible potential class, so the claim should be interpreted with the paper's hypotheses rather than generalized to all monotone potentials.
sections.ranking_evidence: A stated theorem for quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators with a concrete gap-opening method, connecting spectral theory and mathematical physics.

sections.title: Thouless's bandwidth conjecture: a proof by elliptic periods
sections.abstract: The author claims that for the critical rational Harper operator, the denominator times total bandwidth converges uniformly in the reduced numerator to 32 times Catalan's constant divided by π.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims the stated uniform bandwidth limit and a universal limit for the normalized even coarea density (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The critical rational Harper operator; convergence is uniform over reduced numerators as the denominator grows.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is for the critical rational Harper setting and does not, as stated, cover noncritical couplings or general irrational frequencies.
sections.ranking_evidence: A quantitative asymptotic resolution of a named spectral conjecture, cross-listed in mathematical physics and spectral theory and with a period-based derivation described in the abstract.
